findingsForPlanner: Card snapshot correction (quoted at source): src/jobs/conformant.mjs line 509 at 26e0c04 is inside syntheticStagedAtoms (the rate probe), not the flood path; the flood atoms come from src/stages/demote/flood.mjs floodAtomsToStage line 151, which already stamped mapAccessPolicy('public-free') (three-field canonical). Flood rows in the store are therefore not expected to carry the legacy pair; the re-stamp matches on the pair over every entity type, so the dry run will report whatever is there.

The re-stamp keeps atom identity: atomId = contentId({entityType, nodeId, claim, logicVersion}) excludes access, so the in-place UPDATE keeps every atom_did and a writer re-run ON CONFLICT DO UPDATEs the same did with a canonical body. LOGIC_VERSION was deliberately not bumped; bumping it would mint new dids beside the old rows.

Merge sequencing: after this lands, a county's write_stage_atoms in the Factory store still holds legacy bodies from earlier runs. The chunk path merges only rows staged since the chunk, and accessPolicyProjection now refuses a legacy body, so those rows are inert; a whole-stage re-merge for cad-parcel-roll would refuse ACCESS_NOT_CANONICAL until the county is re-staged by a writer run. Named in leave_behind.

src/lib/publish-guards.mjs assertAccessPair is presence-shaped and publish.test.mjs asserts it accepts {public, anonymous}. It reads, it does not produce, so it is outside this card; when the re-stamp closes for the six it should refuse the legacy pair like LDT's guard (F-06 publish card).

The run-row vocabulary finding from card B stands: writeTermination sets runs.status = exit_kind after this job writes 'failed' + refuse_code; the job relies on refuse_code and the termination exit_kind, as bastrop-publish does.
